paragraphs.text: 1 The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake. 2 And he said, “The LORD will roar from Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the habitations of the shepherds shall mourn, and the top of Carmel shall wither.”

“The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel, in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake” [1].

The prophet Amos was not ashamed to highlight his work as a shepherd of sheep in Tekoa, that is, that he came from the poor classes, especially as he was a gatherer of sycamore fruit, which none does but one in great need. As for the absence of his father’s name, it is because he was from a poor and unknown family.

It is remarkable that he says: “The words of Amos… which he saw,” and not which he heard or delivered, affirming that the words he proclaims here are not from himself but are the fruit of divine visions and revelations by the Holy Spirit.
He has specified the place of his upbringing and the date of his prophetic work, two matters which we discussed earlier in the introduction.
He said: “The LORD will roar from Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the habitations of the shepherds shall mourn, and the top of Carmel shall wither” [2].

This is the opening of his prophecy, and perhaps Amos’s dwelling in Tekoa on the edge of the wilderness gave him the experience of the roaring of the lion in the wilderness, which terrifies the shepherds and strikes dread into the life of the farmers. The prophet Amos likened God in His wrath against sin to the lion that roars, saying: “The lion hath roared, who will not fear? the Lord GOD hath spoken, who can but prophesy?” (Amos 3:8). The roaring of the lion does not arise from emptiness, nor is it uttered without cause: “Will a lion roar in the forest, when he hath no prey?” (Amos 3:4).

The prophets Hosea and Joel spoke of God, blessed be His name, as a lion who utters his voice so that heaven and earth tremble, and all realize that He is the refuge of His people and a stronghold for them, dwelling in their midst in His holy mountain in Jerusalem, His sanctuary, so that no stranger comes near them (Joel 3:16-17). He roars and gathers His people from Egypt and Assyria and settles them in their houses (Hos 11:10-11). Here, however, the prophet Amos sees the holy God as a lion couching in Zion, uttering his voice roaring because of the sins of Israel and Judah and all the surrounding nations. He cannot bear sin to approach His sanctuary and surround Him, so He roars and shakes the foundations of sin and shatters the works of the old man; fire goes out of His mouth and burns its palaces and scatters its being!

When the lion utters his voice, the habitations of the shepherds mourn, and the top of Carmel, the most fertile region, withers, for all realize that the voice of the LORD dries up whatever has arisen upon evil, and shatters every fruit of corruption!

The word of the LORD is not spoken for flattery or hypocrisy or wavering between good and evil, but for shattering evil in order to establish good, or crucifying the old man to announce the rising of the new man. The Lion who came out of the tribe of Judah roared, affirming this: “No man putteth a piece of new cloth unto an old garment, for that which is put in to fill it up taketh from the garment, and the rent is made worse. Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runneth out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved” (Mt 9:16-17). As St. Ambrose says: [For this reason the Lord forbids us to mix the new with the old, and the Apostle forbids putting on the new garment over the old; rather we put off the old and put on the new, so that we may not be found naked (2 Cor 5:2-4)].

Jacob realized this when he blessed his son Judah, from whose loins would come forth the Lion who roars against sin and terrifies death, saying: “Judah is a lion’s whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as a lioness; who shall rouse him up?” (Gen 49:9). He saw Him couching as a lion on the Cross, roaring against the sin that corrupted human life in order to kill his prey, the devil and his works, granting humanity sanctification and making it Zion and the holy Jerusalem!

In truth, the prophecy of Amos as a whole is the roaring of the Lion from Zion. It began with terrifying chastisements, the fire that burns the palaces and shatters the fortresses and scatters the inhabitants, whether of the nations or of the Jews, not that they might remain a ruin without inhabitant, but that at the end of the prophecy He might open wide the doors of hope; instead of palaces He raises up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and instead of fortresses He Himself repairs their breaches and raises up their ruins, and builds them as in the days of old and dwells Himself in their midst, so that His name is called upon all the nations (Amos 9:11-12). He pulls down and builds, plucks up and plants, shatters the old man to raise up the new in us! This is the roaring of the Lion from Zion, who utters His voice from Jerusalem, His sanctuary!

3 Thus saith the LORD; “For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron: 4 But I will send a fire into the house of Hazael, which shall devour the palaces of Benhadad. 5 I will break also the bar of Damascus, and cut off the inhabitant from the plain of Aven, and him that holdeth the sceptre from the house of Eden: and the people of Syria shall go into captivity unto Kir, saith the LORD.”

In His chastisements of the nations and Judah He took one course in announcing the One who presents the chastisement, that is, “God Himself,” and their three and four transgressions, and the not turning back from the chastisement, and the sending of a consuming fire… All these shared together in speaking of the chastisement of all the nations and Judah, but each nation was marked by a particular sin or sins of its own.

At the beginning of every chastisement He says: “Thus saith the LORD…” (vv. 3, 6, 9, 11, 13; ch. 2:1, 4, 6). Although not all the nations worship Him, He is the Judge of all, the God of the whole earth, who judges all and cares also for all!
As for His speaking of their three and four transgressions, these two numbers point here to many meanings, of which we mention:

First: the number 3 points to the human soul as being in the image and likeness of the Holy Trinity, and the number 4 points to the body as being taken from the earth with its four directions (east, west, north, south); so it is as though God chastises us for our sins of the soul (such as pride and malice) and the sins of the body (such as love of luxury, gluttony and bodily lusts). As St. Augustine says: [For sins are committed either by the mind, as by the will alone, or by the works of the body also, and then they are visible… For three is the nature of the soul, and four because of the body, since man is composed of both].

Second: St. Jerome sees that the three and four transgressions mean sin that has developed to its third generation and its fourth generation, turning from a mere thought in the mind to its declaration through word, then deed, and finally becoming a habit. God in His long-suffering does not punish a man when sin stirs in his mind, but as it is said: “visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation” (Num 14:18). This means that God does not punish us immediately for our thoughts, but for the evil deeds and the habits of sin that spring from them, as was said by the mouth of Amos: “For three transgressions of the city, such and such, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof.”
Again St. Jerome comments on these three and four transgressions that they are:
a. Thinking evil (the first transgression).
b. Doing evil (the second transgression).
c. Not repenting of it or continuing in it (the third transgression).
d. Teaching it (the fourth transgression).

Among his words: [Now what (the prophet) says is this: You accepted evil and I forgave you; you committed sin and I pardoned you; you did not repent of it and I gave you an excuse; will you also teach sin?! This is what Scripture meant concerning the three and four transgressions].

These are the three and four transgressions from which He does not turn back, but sends a fire that burns the palaces of their evil, the fire of His wrath against sin. He cannot bear sin, but He loves sinners! Perhaps this fire is also the natural fruit of sin, the consuming fire, so God leaves man to reap the fruit of his work, to embrace the fire of his sin, which burns his vain palaces that carry glittering, temporary sights.
This concerns the nations in general; now we speak of each nation separately.

Damascus is the capital of Syria (Aram), and Israel lived for nearly a century in a state of terror of Aram, and some contemporaries of Amos witnessed the war that Hazael king of Aram and his son Benhadad stirred up against Israel (2 Kgs 8:7-15, 28-29; 10:32-33; 13:3-7, 22-25). Gilead, east of the Jordan and north of Syria, was the theatre of this bitter war, which was marked by cruelty and brutality, so that we see Elisha weeping, and when Hazael asks him, before seizing the kingdom, the secret of his weeping, he answers: “Because I know the evil that thou wilt do unto the children of Israel: their strong holds wilt thou set on fire, and their young men wilt thou slay with the sword, and wilt dash their children, and rip up their women with child” (2 Kgs 8:12).
The fruit of this cruelty is:

First: the fire burns the palace of King Hazael, the stirrer of wars, and his son Benhadad [4]. If this king and his son thought themselves able to shatter the kingdom of God and occupy it, God with the fire of His justice returns their work upon them, so the fire of their evil turns back upon their palace, the center of their authority, the place of their planning, and the place of their security and safety… and it burns and is destroyed.

In bitterness I say that our inner Hazael is the “human Ego,” which occupies the heart as its palace, and it and the evils it begets (Benhadad) set about using man with all his energies, potentials, gifts and abilities to work on behalf of evil, instead of the Lord reigning in the heart so that man may work as instruments of righteousness for God. In truth, while the “I” thinks that it is able to reign and rule and dwell securely in its inner palace, it brings upon itself a fire that burns its potentials and loses all its authority.

Then let us leave our inner palace to our Lord Jesus instead of Hazael and Benhadad, to be His dwelling and the center of His kingdom, our Lord declaring His Kingdom in it with power, so that the fires of sin, especially the “I,” cannot approach it because it is aflame with heavenly fire, with the Holy Spirit Himself, who shapes it from day to day that it may reach the measure of the fullness of Christ, and takes it from glory to glory, to enter with it in Christ Jesus into the bosom of the Father, and it will rest there forever!
Let us surrender our palace to the heavenly King with His fiery Spirit, so that Hazael no longer dwells in us with his son Benhadad.

Second: He broke the impregnable fortresses that surround Damascus, not that man may live without fortresses, but that instead of fortresses of stone the Lord Himself may be found as his stronghold and the refuge of his life. For when human arms of stone are present, man leans on them; therefore the Lord shatters them to give us the eternal arms instead, and says: “I will love thee, O LORD, my strength. The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my rock, in whom I will take refuge; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation, and my refuge” (Ps 18:1-2).

Let the transient walls of stone of Damascus be pulled down, that God may offer us Himself, the Rock of Ages, a wall of rock that the serpent cannot approach, nor can it deceive us while we are in Him; we enter Him and rest, and He is a blazing divine wall of fire that surrounds us and kindles our depths, so that we may be like the heavenly beings, “his ministers a flaming fire” (Ps 104:4).

Third: the plain of Aven is turned into a ruin without inhabitant, and it is also called the valley of vanity, or the valley of idols… For when evil works in a man, he thinks he has acquired human wisdom able to enrich him, and he gains much at the expense of others, and behold, he sets up in his heart a valley of vanity or a center of idol worship. He buys emptiness with evil, and acquires deprivation through malice and cunning! This is the lot of the wicked, of whom the psalmist said: “For they shall soon be cut down like the grass, and wither as the green herb” (Ps 37:2).

Fourth: every great man “that holdeth the sceptre” dies in the house of Eden, or in the house of delight and luxury, so that man loses in it everything great and everything strong through his absorption in temporal pleasures and luxuries.
Fifth: the captivity of the Arameans to Kir, the kingdom of the Medes, which was fulfilled historically as is recorded in (2 Kgs 16:9; Isa 22:5-6).

Who are these Arameans, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, over whom Hazael and his son Benhadad reign, but the energies of man and his abilities and his psychological, mental (intellectual) and bodily gifts?! For when Hazael, that is, the “I,” reigns over them, they turn into slavery and work on behalf of the kingdom of the Medes. Man loses his energies, not that he lives without them, but he lives with energies that have been directed to evil and have deviated from their exalted mission. Man with all his potentials turns to work on behalf of the enemy of good under the slavery of the devil, instead of lifting them up by the Holy Spirit on behalf of the kingdom of God!

In short, the fruit of what Hazael and his son Benhadad did, that is, the fruit of pride and self-reliance, is that man loses his inner palace, and his fortresses to which he fled are pulled down, and he loses all greatness and strength as in the house of Aven, and acquires deprivation in the house of delight, and all his energies are taken captive on behalf of the enemy of good! In other words, he loses his authority (his palace), his peace (his fortresses), his delight (in the house of Eden) and all his energies!

This is what the Lord meant by the chastisement of Damascus… that man may realize what complete deprivation and total destruction he has reached, and so flee to God alone, who restores to him what he lost, doubled, on a supreme heavenly level!

6 Thus saith the LORD; “For three transgressions of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they carried away captive the whole captivity, to deliver them up to Edom: 7 But I will send a fire on the wall of Gaza, which shall devour the palaces thereof: 8 And I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod, and him that holdeth the sceptre from Ashkelon, and I will turn mine hand against Ekron: and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish, saith the Lord GOD.”

Gaza was the capital of Philistia at that time, and the sin of Philistia at that time was their exploitation of the sons of Judah who fled to them from before Sennacherib king of Assyria, seizing them and selling them as slaves to the sons of Edom, their bitterest enemies. They wanted to wipe out the name of Israel at that time, as the psalmist says: “They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance” (Ps 83:4). Therefore the fire that turned back upon them was to devour the palaces of the principal cities: Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon and Ekron.

St. Augustine sees that the word Philistines means “those who fall from drunkenness,” and so it points to the souls that become drunk with the love of the world and its luxury. St. Jerome interprets this name as “death by a poisonous draught,” and in his view they represent those who drink the cup of Satan’s seduction as a poison for the soul that destroys it, so that they fall quickly.

9 Thus saith the LORD; “For three transgressions of Tyrus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly covenant: 10 But I will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus, which shall devour the palaces thereof.”
Phoenicia, whose capital was Tyre, took pride in its navy and its enormous trade on a strong international level.

Tyre forgot the treaty of brotherhood between their king Hiram and King Solomon (1 Kgs 5:1-12; 9:10-14), and sold the Israelites who fled to them as slaves to their enemy Edom. Therefore God allowed the fires to burn their palaces for the betrayal of the brotherly covenant, and this was fulfilled literally when Nebuchadnezzar besieged it and captured it in the sixth century B.C.

St. Jerome and St. Augustine see that the word “Tyre” means distress or trial. Therefore what is said about Tyre, especially in the Book of Ezekiel (chapter 28), points to Satan, who pushes people into satanic trials and temptations.

11 Thus saith the LORD; “For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever: 12 But I will send a fire upon Teman, which shall devour the palaces of Bozrah.”

Edom is Esau, the brother of Jacob, and the sons of Edom took a hostile position toward the sons of Israel (Jacob) when they passed through the wilderness, for they did not allow them to pass (Num 20:13-21), and they always stood in a position of gloating over the sons of Israel, and sometimes even carried out destructive attacks.
The word “Edom” is taken from “Adam,” and means “a bloody man,” or “earthly,” and points to the love of shedding blood for the sake of earthly things.

If Edom was inflamed with the fire of evil and the love of shedding blood, the fire turns back upon him to burn the palaces of the most important of his regions, Teman (Teman is a tribe named after the firstborn of Eliphaz the son of Esau), and the regions it inhabits (Gen 36:11, 15, 42). The region lies in the north of Edom (Ezek 35:13), and its inhabitants were known for your wisdom (Jer 49:7).

As for Bozrah, whose palaces are burned, it is a city in the land of Edom (Isa 34:6; 63:1). The word “Bozrah” means in Hebrew “fortress” or “sheepfold,” and it was utterly ruined as the prophet Jeremiah prophesied concerning it (Jer 49:13)… If Bozrah, with its potentials, represents the fortress of Teman in Edom, then evil burns its goods and destroys its potentials and makes it a ruin.

entries.section: 6. The chastisement of the children of Ammon:

paragraphs.text: 13 Thus saith the LORD; “For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border: 14 But I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it shall devour the palaces thereof, with shouting in the day of battle, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind: 15 And their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together, saith the LORD.”

In our study of the Book of Ezekiel we saw that the children of Ammon, the descendants of Ben-ammi the son of Lot (Gen 19:38), were hard of heart and offered their children as sacrifices to the god Milcom (1 Kgs 11:5-33). They were in constant war with the sons of Israel.

The sons of Ammon represent cruelty based on greed: “because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border” [13]. Thus greed corrupts the humanity of man and his natural tenderness, for the sake of an earthly gain the womb of pregnant women is ripped open, killing them and tormenting them and making them lose their unborn children! A hideous picture of the heart that the earth turns into a predatory beast, having no mercy on the weak women or on the unborn children, who have no guilt and no strength!

As for its natural fruit, the fires devour the walls of its capital Rabbah (Amman) and burn its palaces, and it turns into a region of battle and tempests, and its king and his great men are taken captive. If “Rabbah” means “great,” then the man who is cruel to others and shatters them for his own earthly benefit, to be great over all and richer than all, loses his walls and his palaces are burned and his inner life turns into a field of bitter battle, and he loses his true peace, and his mind and heart and all his energies are taken captive to what belongs to the enemy. He comes to a state of complete loss of everything! For while he thinks that he is acquiring by his strength and power, behold, he enters into a severe emptiness, and a loss even of his life and his peace and his potentials!

1 Thus saith the LORD; "For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime: 2 But I will send a fire upon Moab, and it shall devour the palaces of Kerioth: and Moab shall die with tumult, with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet: 3 And I will cut off the judge from the midst thereof, and will slay all the princes thereof with him, saith the LORD."

In our study of the book of Ezekiel we saw that Moab descended from Lot by his elder daughter, and that he was called "Moab" because his mother bore him by her own father, since the word "Moab" means "from the father." St. Jerome sees that the elder daughter took advantage of her father's drunkenness and bore Moab by him, that he might point to Satan and to all who depart from God their Father and do not think of Him. St. Augustine sees that the sons of Moab point to whoever uses the Law in an unlawful, sinful manner, so that they stumble in it, just as Lot's daughter used her father in a sinful manner.

The crime of the sons of Moab is that they stole the bones of the king of Edom and burned them to turn them into lime. Although this seems a simple crime, God hates sin, however small its measure may be in our eyes. It is remarkable that the bones belonged to a king who was an enemy of the people of God, yet God does not love cruelty or violence, even when it is directed against dead enemies.

The fruit of this cruelty is that He returns the fire of their cruelty upon their most fortified city, "Kerioth," which was perhaps the capital of Moab (it is Khirbet al-Rabbah, 14 miles south of the river Arnon). He turns Moab into a war zone that dies at the sound of the trumpet, and He deprives it of the judge in its midst, so that there is neither justice nor wisdom in it, and He slays its princes.
What Moab did to the dead bones, with an evil soul and a hard heart, returns upon its cities, its princes and its people!

4 Thus saith the LORD; "For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have despised the law of the LORD, and have not kept his commandments, and their lies caused them to err, after the which their fathers have walked: 5 But I will send a fire upon Judah, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem."

If the word "Judah" means "confession," then those who ought to have declared their faith and confessed it through their obedience to the divine commandment are themselves the ones who "despised the law of the LORD, and have not kept his commandments, and their lies caused them to err, after the which their fathers have walked" [4]. Instead of confessing the truth, they accepted falsehood and walked after errors and lies!

What grieves the soul is that the fire turns back to burn the palaces of Jerusalem. If Jerusalem means "the vision of God," then turning away from God's commandment and running after errors corrupts the inner sight, so that it does not behold God. For this reason the Lord says: "Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God" (Mt 5:8). As St. Augustine says: [Let us purify our hearts by faith, that we may be made ready for Him who cannot be described, that is, for the unseen vision]. He also says: [All that the divine Holy Scriptures present aims only at purifying the inner sight, which hinders it from seeing God. Just as the eye was created to see this temporal light, so that if a foreign body enters it, it clouds its clearness and separates it from seeing that light, so also is the eye of your heart: if it is clouded and wounded, it turns away from the light of righteousness and does not dare or manage to look at it... And what clouds the clearness of the eye of your heart? Lust, covetousness, iniquity and worldly pleasure; all this clouds the eye of the heart, closes it and blinds it].

6 Thus saith the LORD; "For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of shoes; 7 That pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor, and turn aside the way of the meek: and a man and his father will go in unto the same maid, to profane my holy name: 8 And they lay themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar, and they drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their god. 9 Yet destroyed I the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedars, and he was strong as the oaks; yet I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots from beneath. 10 Also I brought you up from the land of Egypt, and led you forty years through the wilderness, to possess the land of the Amorite. 11 And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith the LORD. 12 But ye gave the Nazarites wine to drink; and commanded the prophets, saying, Prophesy not. 13 Behold, I am pressed under you, as a cart is pressed that is full of sheaves. 14 Therefore the flight shall perish from the swift, and the strong shall not strengthen his force, neither shall the mighty deliver himself: 15 Neither shall he stand that handleth the bow; and he that is swift of foot shall not deliver himself: neither shall he that rideth the horse deliver himself. 16 And he that is courageous among the mighty shall flee away naked in that day, saith the LORD."
Before presenting sermons to Israel, He revealed to them the secret of their chastisement, showing three matters:
First: The injustice they practice [6-8].
Second: Their meeting God's kindnesses to them with ingratitude [9-12].
Third: All of them falling under chastisement [13-16].
"Thus saith the LORD; For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of shoes" [6].

Perhaps this is the first written accusation that a prophet from among the "writing prophets" directs against Israel in the name of the Lord Himself: "they sold the righteous for silver." Who is this righteous one who was sold for silver but the Lord Christ, who alone is righteous, without sin, whom Judas the traitor sold for thirty pieces of silver, the price of a slave (Mt 27:5; Lk 22:5), He who bought us not with gold or silver, but with His precious blood? The Lord offered His life as a ransom for the slave, and the slave sold his Lord for silver, betraying Him. In bitterness the prophet Zechariah says: "So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver. And the LORD said unto me, Cast it unto the potter: a goodly price that I was prised at of them" (Zech 11:12-13). This is the goodly price at which the Lord was priced!

It is the sin of all generations: Israel sells the Lord for thirty pieces of silver, since the silver of the world rises in its eyes above life with the Lord, and it values temporal things above divine things!

What does the selling of the poor for a pair of shoes [6] also mean? Who is this needy one who is sold for a pair of shoes but the Lord Christ, who presents Himself to us through the suffering, the needy and the poor?! God asked His prophet Moses to take off his shoes, so that he might be able to enter into the divine holy things, behold the mysteries of God, enter with Him into a friendly conversation, and receive the pastoral work (Ex 3). For the same reason the Lord asked His disciples not to have shoes (Mt 10:10), so that they would not walk as earthly men who walk on the ground in shoes, but would lift their hearts up to heaven and draw with them, by the Holy Spirit, every heart to where Christ is seated. But man in his folly, instead of taking off his shoes to live in the heavens and to rise to the divine things, sells the poor man, "Christ Himself," for a pair of shoes, preferring rather to be bound to earthly things and to walk in temporal things, instead of being freed from shoes and living in heavenly things.

Origen sees in the shoes a reference to the dead temporal life and to the love of display. For shoes are made from the skin of dead animals, which is also used in drums that give out sounds without any work. Thus the Lord Christ, with His eternal glory, is sold for the sake of the dead temporal life, or for the acquiring of vain temporal honor that has a glittering appearance without serious inner work!
The Lord went on to reveal strange examples of the abominations that the Israelites were committing, in which uncleanness in its most hideous forms was mingled with injustice, namely:

A. "That pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor" [7], and in some translations, "they trample the head of the poor down to the dust of the earth!" Not only do they show no pity to their poor brethren, but in the coarseness of their hearts they wrong them, dragging their heads down to the dust in order to tread on them with their feet.

Who is this head of the poor on whom they tread with their feet but the Lord Christ Himself, the Head of the whole Church? They despise Him and make light of His precious salvation. As the Apostle Paul says: "Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?" (Heb 10:29).

When we despise the poor man and treat him lightly, we are only despising his Head, Christ Jesus Himself. For this reason St. John Chrysostom says: [How great is the rank of the poor, for they are like the chamber of God, in which the righteous One is hidden! The poor man stretches out his hand begging, but it is God who receives your alms]. He also says in the person of the Lord: [It has reached you about Me that I am clothed with light as with a garment, but when you clothe a naked man I feel warmth and I am covered!].

B. "And turn aside the way of the meek" [7], that is, they close the road before the suffering... They do not stop at passivity, that is, ignoring the needy and sorrowful man, but if they find an open road before him for his salvation, they close it. They are volunteers working for the kingdom of injustice.

C. "And a man and his father will go in unto the same maid, to profane my holy name" [7]. It is a hideous picture of abominations that a man and his father should share in the sin of fornication with one young maiden! As St. Basil the Great says in his letter to Diodorius: [The Law never mentioned a man and his father committing fornication with a young maiden, because it is a hideous matter that needs no warning against, just as the Apostle Paul said: "But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not be once named among you, as becometh saints" (Eph 5:3)].

D. "And they lay themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar, and they drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their god" [8]. The matter does not stop at their staying by the pagan altars and sharing in the feasts of the house of the strange gods; rather, this abominable work was mingled with cruelty. While they pretend piety as they lie down beside every altar, behold they lie down upon the clothes of the poor, who pledged them with them and were unable to pay the amount and receive back the clothes, and they drink the wine of those who have financial fines and are unable to pay what is owed by them!! They worship using the clothes and wine of the poor who are unable to obtain the basic necessities of life!

entries.section: Second: Their meeting God's kindnesses to them with ingratitude [9-12]:

paragraphs.text: Having listed bitter pictures and examples of the abominations of the Israelites, mingled with injustice and cruelty, He wished to affirm that they are without excuse, since God had shown them many kindnesses, and instead of repaying them with a holy and gentle life, behold, they walk in ingratitude.

"Yet destroyed I the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedars, and he was strong as the oaks; yet I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots from beneath. Also I brought you up from the land of Egypt, and led you forty years through the wilderness, to possess the land of the Amorite. And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith the LORD. But ye gave the Nazarites wine to drink; and commanded the prophets, saying, Prophesy not" [9-12].
It is the constant story of man: in every generation God offers salvation, declaring His surpassing divine love for man, and man in the folly of his heart meets love with ingratitude!

From the historical side, God prepared the way for Israel of old. Since the Amorites were giants like the cedar and strong like the oak, God broke their fruit and uprooted their roots from the depths, and set out with His people from the land of Egypt, carried as if on the wings of His surpassing love, caring for them throughout their stay in the wilderness for forty years, until He delivered to them the land of the Amorites. And the sign of His love for them is that He made prophets for Himself from among them, and from their young men Nazarites consecrated in His name! But they met love with hatred, and God's gifts with ingratitude and disobedience. The sign of this is that they asked the Nazarites to drink wine, and commanded the prophets not to utter a word of the Lord. As St. John Chrysostom says: [God accused the Israelites, showing that they deserve a greater chastisement because they sinned after He had granted them such great honors].

It is remarkable that He put the giving of wine to the Nazarites before their commanding the prophets not to utter the word of the Lord and His prophecies, because drinking wine signifies man's loss of his balance and wisdom, so that he serves the house of the Lord in a state of drunkenness, which corrupts the house of God and destroys its peace. As St. Jerome says: [Aaron and the other priests used to abstain from every strong drink when they entered the temple, lest they die. This teaches us that those who serve in the Church without reverence die]. If compelling the prophets to stop bearing witness to God by proclaiming the word of prophecy is a grave sin, how much more so for one who enters the house of God and not only stands silent about the truth, but in irreverence confuses the truth, corrupts the sanctuary of God and hinders the spiritual work.

Let us return once more to God's work with Israel, to see His work with each one of us. The Amorite whom He destroyed before us is none other than the enemy of good, the devil, who ruled the earth for a time. He appeared like a giant like the cedar and strong like the oak, so we feared him and dreaded him, but the Lord by His cross broke his authority, and by the preaching of Him He saw him fallen from heaven like lightning (Lk 10:18). The Lord brought us up, as it were, from the land of bondage, carrying us by His Holy Spirit to inherit the land that the Amorite had ruled for a time, so that we became kings and priests to the Lord. May we not do what the Israelites did, drinking of the wine of the world and ceasing from the spirit of prophecy, or witness, for the Lord.

entries.section: Third: All of them falling under chastisement [13-16]:

paragraphs.text: The Lord affirms that, since they sinned, there is no possibility of escaping chastisement, and He began His speech by saying: "Behold, I am pressed under you, as a cart is pressed that is full of sheaves" [13]. In many translations: "Behold, I press from under you, as the full cart presses." It is as though God complains of the weight of our sins, which press upon Him, as though we were a cart full of sheaves.

God, who upholds the whole world by the word of His power, groans because of our sins and iniquities! He says: "I cannot away with; it is iniquity, even the solemn meeting. Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hateth: they are a trouble unto me; I am weary to bear them" (Isa 1:13-14). Again, when He sees His people turning back from Him, He says in bitterness: "Mine heart is turned within me" (Hos 11:8).

May we not be like the cart full of sheaves of evil, which weighs upon the soul and heart of our heavenly Father and presses upon our Redeemer who said: "My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death... O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me" (Mt 26:38-39). Rather, let us be God's chariot of fire, bearing His heavenly nature working in us, so that we do not represent a weight and pressure upon Him, but fly by the Spirit of the Holy God, soaring in the heavenly places, rising from glory to glory without hindrance!

Instead of being a cart burdened with sheaves of evil, hindering God's saving work, may we be like a light, swift cloud carrying the Lord who rides upon it, heading toward Egypt to set up an altar for Himself in the midst of it (Isa 19).

The Lord continues His speech: "Therefore the flight shall perish from the swift, and the strong shall not strengthen his force, neither shall the mighty deliver himself: Neither shall he stand that handleth the bow; and he that is swift of foot shall not deliver himself: neither shall he that rideth the horse deliver himself. And he that is courageous among the mighty shall flee away naked in that day, saith the LORD" [14-19].

What a harsh and difficult picture! No one, however great his wisdom and abilities, can escape chastisement. "The flight shall perish from the swift," that is, the refuge or escape flees from him who thinks himself quick-witted and able to run away. For at that time, when man falls under the fruit of his sins, his intellectual ability to act (swiftly) at that time does not rescue him, nor does the strength of the body strengthen him, nor the heroism for which he was famous, nor the bow in his hands, nor the horse he rides, nor the strength of heart for which he was known... He cannot be saved, but stands naked, because he is found not clothed with "Christ," our righteousness!

May we possess "Christ Jesus" our Lord within us. He alone is the One whom we put on, and He covers us; we enter into Him and are sheltered; we hold His cross like a strong bow that never fails; our feet are strengthened so that we walk the way of truth, and we have the possibility of setting out not by a horse but by a heavenly chariot, and our heart is strengthened by Him, so that the day of the Lord is turned into a day of joy and victory. Our Jesus alone is our strength, our victory, our spiritual weapon, our eternal garment, our glory and our joy that is not taken away from us.

In ancient times the work of the Law was to declare the futility of all our human possibilities for salvation, not that we might live crushed, but that we might receive our Christ as the true source of our salvation.

The psalmist looked at those around him, hoping he might find help in the princes, but he realized their weakness, for he says: "Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of man, in whom there is no help. His breath goeth forth, he returneth to his earth" (Ps 146:3). In bitterness he found no possibility of salvation even in his parents: "When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up" (Ps 27:10). And since he found no helper in all mankind, he said: "I said in my haste, All men are liars" (Ps 116:10). And if a man thinks himself mighty or a man of abilities, the Lord rebukes him: "Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, let not the rich man glory in his riches" (Jer 9:23). And if he relies on his horse, he hears: "An horse is a vain thing for safety" (Ps 33:17); "But ye said, No; for we will flee upon horses; therefore shall ye flee: and, We will ride upon the swift; therefore shall they that pursue you be swift" (Isa 30:16).
Therefore let us accept God Himself as our Savior, our wisdom, our riches, our strength, and everything to us!

entries.section: 1. He punishes them because they are His people:

paragraphs.text: 1 Hear this word that the LORD hath spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, 2 "You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities." [1-2.]

By this introduction God, as it were, summons them to His court, declaring that He is the competent authority. He calls all the people, as the whole family that went down to Egypt and was delivered from there; He knew it by name, cared for it and called it by His name, apart from all the other families of the earth. This love and this care do not mean that He closes His eyes to their faults; rather, they place upon them all the more responsibility, for He does not accept fellowship with guilty people. He knew them and they knew Him, for it is said, "In Judah is God known" (Ps 76:1). Therefore their responsibility is greater, as the Lord says: "And that servant, which knew his lord's will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes. But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes. For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more" (Lk 12:47-48). The more our knowledge of God's will, His mysteries and the works of His surpassing love increases, the more is demanded of us, and our responsibility before Him is greater than that of others. As St. Cyril the Great says: [The crime is not a matter for discussion in the case of one who knew his master's will and neglects it, and does not do what is fitting, although it is his duty to do so.]

entries.section: 2. He does not punish without cause:

paragraphs.text: 3 Can two walk together, except they be agreed? 4 Will a lion roar in the forest, when he hath no prey? will a young lion cry out of his den, if he have taken nothing? 5 Can a bird fall in a snare upon the earth, where no gin is for him? shall one take up a snare from the earth, and have taken nothing at all? 6 Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid? shall there be evil in a city, and the LORD hath not done it? 7 Surely the Lord GOD will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets. 8 The lion hath roared, who will not fear? the Lord GOD hath spoken, who can but prophesy?

Since God has brought His people to trial before Him, because He is the competent authority, He is like a lion roaring, a sign that they deserve judgment, for God does not seek to try His people without cause. The Lord has set out the proof through seven questions that reveal that there is no room for God to be angry without cause... and that at the same time, as He judges, He enters into a shared conversation with them, explaining to them the secrets of His trial, for "he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets" [7.]
The seven questions are:
"Can two walk together, except they be agreed?!
Will a lion roar in the forest, when he hath no prey?!
Will a young lion cry out of his den, if he have taken nothing?!
Can a bird fall in a snare upon the earth, where no gin is for him?!
Shall one take up a snare from the earth, and have taken nothing at all?!
Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid?!
Shall there be evil in a city, and the LORD hath not done it?!" [3-6.]

If all the answers to the preceding questions are negative, He continues in the same manner: "Surely the Lord GOD will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets. The lion hath roared, who will not fear?! The Lord GOD hath spoken, who can but prophesy?!" [7-8.]

This speech has revealed that the trial that is taking place is not an imaginary matter but a serious and grave one, a reality that is fulfilled not without causes, but because the measure has overflowed concerning what the people committed against the Holy One and against themselves. These seven examples revealed important and grave aspects touching God's relationship with His people, because of which the trial takes place, the most important of which are:

First: The need for a new covenant, for He opens His speech by saying: "Can two walk together, except they be agreed" (or unless there is between them an appointment and an agreement)?! Certainly not! How then can God and man walk together, when the people of God have broken the covenant and violated the agreement?! The Lord says: "And if ye will not be reformed by me by these things, but will walk contrary unto me; Then will I also walk contrary unto you, and will punish you yet seven times for your sins" (Lev 26:23-24). If the people violate the covenant, how can God walk with them?! For this reason the need became urgent to establish a new covenant in which God is reconciled with His people.

This is what the Lord declared by the prophet Jeremiah: "Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt; which my covenant they brake, and I rejected them, saith the LORD: But this shall be the covenant... I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people" (Jer 31:31-33). This was fulfilled on Covenant Thursday, when the Lord Christ gave us His Body, given for us, as a new covenant, in which we meet with the Father by our union with Him in His Son Jesus the Crucified. We enjoy the Body broken for us and the Blood shed for our salvation as a new covenant, in which our sonship to the Father is established, and His fatherhood to us, by our union in the Body of His only-begotten Son! Truly, in Christ Jesus the Sacrifice we meet with the Father and walk together, for we have agreed together in the mind of His Son and His eternal covenant.

Second: God declares that in the trial He knows no slackness. In His justice He leaves us to the evil that we have acquired for ourselves by our freedom, so that He is like the lion that roars in the forest, where rugged and fruitless humanity, like a dry desert, has become prey to be devoured. And He is like the young lion that seizes the prey offered to it to take a portion of it... We have become prey, and there is no escape from the roaring of the lion and the cry of the young lion except by taking refuge in the Cross, to see the Lion that comes out of Judah roaring not against us but against our sins, not to devour us but to crush the devil our enemy! Let us flee from the divine wrath that roars because of our accepting the enemy, by fleeing to God our Savior, who redeems us from this enemy!

Third: When He presents to us the example of the bird that falls because of the presence of a snare, or the snare that is taken up because it has caught a bird, the Lord is declaring that in the trial we are like the bird fallen in a snare. Can we save ourselves?! By the Lord our Redeemer we say: "Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence" (Ps 91:3). "Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers: the snare is broken, and we are escaped. Our help is in the name of the LORD, who made heaven and earth" (Ps 124:7-8). St. Jerome says: [What is the snare that was broken? The Apostle says: "(The Lord) shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly" (Rom 16:20), "that you may recover yourselves out of the snare of the devil" (2 Tim 2:26). You see that Satan is the fowler, who longs to catch our souls for destruction. Satan is the master of many snares and deceptions of every kind... But when we are in a state of grace our souls are safe, whereas as soon as we play with sin our souls are troubled and become like a ship beaten by the waves.] He also says: [Just as the Lord casts the net and catches a great number of fish, and His disciples, like fishermen, gather through themselves those who accept faith in Him and bring them to Him, so also the devil has his demons subject to him, who set nets for men and lead them to him.]

St. Augustine presents to us the secret of our escaping from the snare: [Because the Lord is in the soul itself, therefore the soul escaped thus like a bird from the snare of the fowlers... Let the Lord be within you, and He will save you from greater threats, from the snare of the fowlers... The snare will be broken, be sure of this, for the pleasures of the present life will not last when their final destiny is fulfilled. Therefore let us not be entangled by them, so that when the snare is broken we may rejoice, saying: The snare is broken, and we are escaped. And lest you think that you can do this by your own strength, look at who works for your deliverance and say: "Our help is in the name of the LORD, who made heaven and earth"...]

Fourth: He says: "Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid?!" It is a state of constant spiritual warfare! As long as we are in the world, the enemy does not cease to oppose us until he seizes us from the Kingdom of God into the kingdom of his darkness. Therefore the Lord sends His servants to blow constantly the trumpet of the Gospel until the final victory is achieved. The Apostle Paul says: "Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might. Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places" (Eph 6:10-12).

St. Augustine says: [Let us look at two enemies: the enemy whom we see and the enemy whom we do not see. The man we see; Satan we do not see. Let us love the man and beware of Satan. Let us pray for the man, and let us pray against Satan.] He gives the reason for this: "For when we suffer from the men who trouble us, it is only because they are vessels of Satan; he uses them and inflames them as vessels that he moves for his own account."

Fifth: The Lord declares that He is the One who permits the trial for the sake of chastisement. "Shall there be evil (calamity) in a city, and the LORD hath not done it?!" The Fathers spoke much about the word "evil" occurring here or in similar expressions, distinguishing between two kinds of evil: the evil that is evil by its nature and contrary to virtue or goodness, and the evil that is pain or distress that we ourselves consider evil. This is what St. John Chrysostom affirmed in more than one place, and as Father John of Damascus says: [He does not mean by these words that God is the cause of evil, but that the word "evil" is used in two ways, with two meanings. Sometimes it means what is evil by nature, which is contrary to virtue and contrary to the will of God, and sometimes it means what is evil and distress to our feeling, that is, sorrows and calamities. These seem evil because they are painful, though in truth they are good, for to those who understand they are a whistle (alarm) calling to conversion and salvation. Of these the Scripture says that "God is their source."] As Father Theodore says: [When the divine judgment speaks with men, it speaks with them according to their human language and feelings. The physician cuts or cauterizes those who suffer from sores for the sake of the soundness of their health, and yet those who are unable to endure it see it as evil.]

Sixth: God declares that if He is the One who permits the chastisement, He "revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets." This is what we see in all the books of the prophets, that God does not deal in a dictatorial manner, commanding and forbidding, but reveals His secrets and reasons with them. For this reason He often repeats Himself in His speeches, because of man's weakness, so that he may grasp the unfathomable mysteries and God's high purposes as far as man is able to receive them.

God loves man and speaks with him as one equal to another. When He wanted to burn Sodom and Gomorrah, He said: "Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do?" (Gen 18:17). And He gave Abraham the opportunity to converse about Sodom and Gomorrah, until Abraham said to Him: "Wilt thou also destroy the righteous with the wicked?... Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?" (Gen 18:23-25). The Lord was not angry with him, but continued the conversation as though he were His friend and equal!! And in more than one place He declares, "Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD"... He wants conversation with man in order to reveal His secret to the upright who fear Him. For it is said: "His secret is with the righteous" (Prov 3:32), "The secret of the LORD is with them that fear him; and he will shew them his covenant" (Ps 25:14).

entries.section: 2. He does not punish without cause:

paragraphs.text: Seventh: Finally the Lord reproaches them: "The lion hath roared, who will not fear? the Lord GOD hath spoken, who can but prophesy?" [8]. If God in His love reveals His secret to His prophets, how is it that they in turn do not announce to the people the roaring of the Lion who came out of His tribe, so that they may fear Him, and His words, so that all may prepare to meet Him? The work of the prophets is to deliver the divine message, even if it appears like a burning fire or a roaring lion, so that all may fear and return to God... The goal of all this is that the prophets utter prophecies as a preparatory way for the coming of the Lord.

St. Augustine has a delightful comment on the saying "The lion hath roared, who will not fear?" He says: [Man has been able to tame the lion, so that he does not fear lions once they are tamed, but he cannot tame himself; let him hand himself over to God alone, the tamer of souls. Are you stronger than the lion? For you are in the image of God! What? Can the image of God (that is, man) tame wild beasts, and God cannot tame His image?!] Then let us put our souls in His hands, for He alone is able to tame them.

entries.section: 3. He calls the Gentiles to witness against them:

paragraphs.text: 9 Publish in the palaces at Ashdod, and in the palaces in the land of Egypt, and say, "Assemble yourselves upon the mountains of Samaria, and behold the great tumults in the midst thereof, and the oppressed in the midst thereof. 10 For they know not to do right, saith the LORD, who store up violence and robbery in their palaces. 11 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; An adversary there shall be even round about the land; and he shall bring down thy strength from thee, and thy palaces shall be spoiled."

God wanted their pagan neighbors to bear witness against them: the rich of Ashdod in Philistia (in the Septuagint, Assyria) and the rich of Egypt, the near and the far, to come and witness the seat of judgment. It is as though God found no righteous men among His people to judge between Him and His vineyard, so He resorted to strangers to judge whether there is any injustice in God's judgment toward His people. Perhaps by calling them He also wished that they would come into contact with Him and perceive His holiness and so take warning, for if He judges His people for their sins, would He show partiality toward those who are not His people?! In their presence there is an opportunity for them to review themselves also.

The hideousness of the sins within Samaria, the capital of Israel, has reached not only the holy God, so that He cannot bear it, but even the Gentiles, who bear witness against them for their evil... because the smell of evil has reached them. What bitterness! Instead of the sons of the Kingdom bearing witness against the wicked and condemning them, the wicked have become witnesses against the people of God, seeing in their midst great tumult and confusion instead of the heavenly life of surpassing glory, and within it oppressions instead of justice and righteousness. They turned into storehouses of injustice and robbery, so that they could not do right. The Lord says to the Gentiles about His people: "Assemble yourselves upon the mountains of Samaria, and behold the great tumults in the midst thereof, and the oppressed in the midst thereof. For they know not to do right... who store up violence and robbery in their palaces" [9-10.] Therefore He besieges it with distress from every side and removes from it its strength and authority!

Israel had become like the salt that should have seasoned others, but now that it has become corrupt, with what shall it be salted? "It is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men" (Mt 5:13). In God's eyes Israel was like the high priest who intercedes for the pagan nations; if he sins, who will intercede for him?! It befitted Israel to be the teacher of the Gentiles about salvation, but since it left the faith, what shall its reward be?

All this terrifies the Christian, especially the priest, for the wider our responsibility, the more severe the punishment when we sin. St. John Chrysostom says: [If others fall, perhaps they can obtain pardon, but if the teacher falls, he is without excuse and falls under an extremely harsh vengeance.]

12 Thus saith the LORD; "As the shepherd taketh out of the mouth of the lion two legs, or a piece of an ear; so shall the children of Israel be taken out that dwell in Samaria in the corner of a bed, and in Damascus in a couch. 13 Hear ye, and testify in the house of Jacob, saith the Lord GOD, the God of hosts, 14 That in the day that I shall visit the transgressions of Israel upon him I will also visit the altars of Bethel: and the horns of the altar shall be cut off, and fall to the ground. 15 And I will smite the winter house with the summer house; and the houses of ivory shall perish, and the great houses shall have an end, saith the LORD."

God has presented a wonderful simile in His chastisement of His people. Although He is the Shepherd who seeks every straying sheep and snatches it from the mouth of the lion, even if nothing remains of it but two legs or even a piece of its ear... this surpassing care and wonderful love is also what makes Him search for His people wherever they are, to allow them to go into captivity for the sake of chastisement.

The feelings of many Fathers were stirred before the surpassing pastoral love of God, so that St. Basil said in one of his letters: [Strive to rise from the ground, and remember that you have the Good Shepherd who follows your track and saves you even if nothing remains of you but two legs or a piece of an ear, bringing it out of the mouth of the beast that wounded you. Remember God's mercies, for He heals you with oil and wine. Do not despair of salvation.]

The Lord, who by His love snatches us from the mouth of the lion, is the One who snatches the Israelites from their land, whoever they are, "that dwell in Samaria in the corner of a bed" [12.] And He follows their track even if they flee to Damascus, even in bed; from there He draws them to the land of captivity.

He punishes not for the sake of punishment in itself, but for two things: the removal of idol worship, "I will also visit the altars of Bethel: and the horns of the altar shall be cut off, and fall to the ground," and the shattering of the life of luxury and pampering, of those who bought special houses for summer and others for winter, and built for themselves great and costly houses of ivory!

1 Hear this word, ye kine of Bashan, that are in the mountain of Samaria, which oppress the poor, which crush the needy, which say to their masters, "Bring, and let us drink." 2 The Lord GOD hath sworn by his holiness, "Lo, the days shall come upon you, that he will take you away with hooks, and your posterity with fishhooks. 3 And ye shall go out at the breaches, every cow at that which is before her; and ye shall cast them into the palace, saith the LORD."
"Hear this word, ye kine of Bashan, that are in the mountain of Samaria, which oppress the poor, which crush the needy, which say to their masters, Bring, and let us drink" [1].

"Bashan" is a Hebrew name meaning "level or smooth land." It referred to the half-tribe of Manasseh (Deut 3:13), and lies in the land of Canaan east of the Jordan between Mount Hermon and Gilead (Num 21:33); its soil is exceedingly fertile and its water abundant. It is mentioned in the Holy Bible about 60 times. It was known for its herds (Ps 22:12; Ezek 39:18), which were marked by much fat (Deut 32:14), and was famous for its evergreen oak forests (Isa 2:13; Ezek 27:6; Zech 11:2) down to this day.

Here the Lord likens the people of Israel to the fat and strong cows of Bashan, which graze in rich pastures, and which were marked by their injustice to the poor and their crushing of the needy. The rich of the people and its nobles grazed amid excessive wealth, seizing everything for themselves. And instead of helping the needy and the oppressed, they exploit their poverty, misery and helplessness in order to crush them all the more with injustice and tyranny, so that the rich grows richer in his riches, and the poor in his poverty and misery.

These rich men go to masters as unjust as themselves and say: "Bring, and let us drink," that is, let us get drunk with you in your feasts and enjoy pleasures and lusts amid the crushing of the needy and the tears of the oppressed, as though they find no pleasure in drunkenness unless they mix it with tears and blend it with injustice. As the wise man says: "So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and from the hand of their oppressors there was oppression" (Eccl 1:4).

Some see that the cows of Bashan here are none other than the Israelite women, who had become fat from the multitude of feasts and a life of excessive luxury, and violent. These women who dwell in Samaria ask their men, that is, their masters or "baals" (husbands), to fulfill for them what the great Baal requires. Since the worship of Baal consists essentially of flagrant drunkenness, these "baals" provide drink for their women. It is as though the cows of Bashan are chiefly responsible for the injustice that falls on the poor and the needy, because they incite their husbands to it in order to fulfill their passing pleasures, especially constant, unceasing drunkenness!
What does God do with these unjust cows?

The Lord GOD hath sworn by his holiness: "Lo, the days shall come upon you, that he will take you away with hooks (a hook or grapnel), and your posterity with fishhooks. And ye shall go out at the breaches, every cow at that which is before her; and ye shall cast them into the palace (the fortress, Hermon), saith the LORD" [2-3].
What does the Lord do with them?

First: The Lord swears by His holiness that He intervenes because of what the cows of Bashan did to His needy and poor children in order to fulfill their drinking and pleasures; so He takes them away with hooks, as the Lord says to Sennacherib king of Assyria by the mouth of Isaiah: "Because thy rage against me and thy tumult is come up into mine ears, therefore I will put my hook in thy nose, and my bridle in thy lips, and I will turn thee back by the way by which thou camest" (Isa 37:29; 2 Kgs 19:28).

It seems that the hook was put in the nose of a violent animal in order to drag it in humiliation, especially wild animals such as lions. Therefore it was used to drag captives, especially kings, to humiliate them, as the king of Assyria did to Manasseh (2 Chr 33:11). Since the cows of Bashan raged against the poor for the sake of their pleasures, God drags them away as captives; He seizes them and puts hooks in their noses so that they become captives without honor, authority or strength!

The world in its pleasures plays with man and makes him like a wild animal, thinking that no one escapes from his hands and fangs, but he soon finds himself led in humiliation to where he tastes the fruit of his injustice.
Second: The chastisement does not stop at the cows, but He catches their children like fish with the fishhook! Man in his revelry prepares loss, even destruction, for his children as well.

If the children of Israel represent the human soul, then their women, that is, the cows of Bashan, point to the body, which falls in humiliation with the soul and is shattered, while the children point to man's gifts, which go down with sin, so that man loses his spirit, his body and all his gifts and energies because of sin. On the contrary, the soul of the righteous rejoices, his body is sanctified and his gifts grow, as the psalmist says: "Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine by the sides of thine house: thy children like olive plants round about thy table. Behold, that thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the LORD" (Ps 128:3-4). He is blessed, and his wife and his children, that is, his soul, his body and all his gifts!

Third: Each cow goes out at the breaches straight before her, to rush into the fortress, or the palace, or Hermon (according to the Greek text). Perhaps the breaches occurred in the walls, since the cows of Bashan, by their injustice and uncleanness, refused to remain within the walls of the divine commandment, and fled through the breaches so as not to meet the commandment, and rushed to the palace they had made for themselves, or the fortress that is the work of their hands, hoping that it might be able to protect them, as man did of old when he tried to build the tower of Babel to hide in it from the face of God at the Flood!

If the Greek text mentions "Hermon" instead of the fortress, perhaps the breaches here mean that the cows of Bashan who did injustice against the needy fall into captivity when the walls of Samaria are split and collapse. They then find no escape but are taken into captivity as to slaughter, and the enemy takes them to Hermon, where the captivity is, or to the palace or the fortress, to remain there as humiliated captives.

entries.section: 2. The rejection of worship joined with injustice:

paragraphs.text: 4 "Come to Bethel, and transgress; at Gilgal multiply transgression; and bring your sacrifices every morning, and your tithes every three days: 5 And offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving with leaven, and proclaim and publish the free offerings: for this liketh you, O ye children of Israel, saith the Lord GOD.

Perhaps the children of Israel think that these warnings do not concern them, for they go to Bethel to offer sacrifices every morning, and pay their tithes every three days without delay, and offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving to God... In their own eyes they are lovers of God, offering Him gifts and offerings without number!

How easy it is for man to deceive himself, treating his evil not by repentance and returning to God but by stopping at some outward forms of worship, so that they deprive the ritual of the Church of its spirit by isolating it from the practical life of faith, and distort the offerings and gifts by presenting them without the heart!
"Come to Bethel, and transgress; at Gilgal multiply transgression" [4].

The Lord says this in the language of irony, for they commit all evils and injustices and go to the holy places and fill them... as though they were a people marked by religiosity and spirituality! They go to holy things while not holy. They visit the house of God and do not return to God Himself! Therefore He says to them: "transgress... and multiply transgression," as though He were saying: if your many visits to the holy places are a cover for your hidden evils, you are adding sin to sin, and treating wounds with more dangerous wounds!
"Bring your sacrifices every morning, and your tithes every three days" [4].

The Jew was bound to offer a yearly sacrifice (1 Sam 1:3, 7, 21), and to present the accounts of his tithes every three years (Deut 14:28; 26:12). If the unjust man offers a daily sacrifice instead of the yearly one, and gives his tithes every three days instead of every three years, he is not accepted by God... For God is not bribed by offerings and money, but seeks the spirit of the gift, the inner fruit in the heart, not the gift in itself. As St. Paul says to the people of Philippi, who were full of love: "Ye sent once and again unto my necessity. Not because I desire a gift: but I desire fruit that may abound to your account" (Phil 4:16-17). For this very reason the same Apostle warns us against giving without love, saying: "And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing" (1 Cor 13:3).

entries.section: 2. The rejection of worship joined with injustice:

paragraphs.text: "And offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving with leaven, and proclaim and publish the free offerings: for this liketh you, O ye children of Israel, saith the Lord GOD" [5]. It is as though He says: if you come to my house and my holy places, and offer sacrifices and pay tithes, you have loved to provoke me, for you offer leaven as a thank offering, and the free offerings to my house. The Law forbade offering leaven: "No meat offering, which ye shall bring unto the LORD, shall be made with leaven: for ye shall burn no leaven, nor any honey, in any offering of the LORD made by fire" (Lev 2:11). Leaven signified the evil that spreads like leaven in the dough; thus, while they present the offerings, they carry their evil in the midst of them, as though it were a thank offering... though in reality it is an offering of provocation to the Lord.

In the Septuagint: "They read the Law outside, and call to public assemblies." Perhaps He means by this that they pretend to religiosity by speaking about the divine Law with unbelievers, and argue with them about it with great zeal, and confirm this zeal by calling to public assemblies. In contrast, they do not carry the Law in their hearts within, and they have no personal relationship with God! This is the most dangerous form of religiosity, when it is all poured into zeal without inner life, and into participation in communal worship and religious celebrations without the hidden relationship with God in the soul or in the closet! This is what the children of Israel loved, as the Lord says.

6 "And I also have given you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and want of bread in all your places: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the LORD. 7 And also I have withholden the rain from you, when there were yet three months to the harvest: and I caused it to rain upon one city, and caused it not to rain upon another city: one piece was rained upon, and the piece whereupon it rained not withered. 8 So two or three cities wandered unto one city, to drink water; but they were not satisfied: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the LORD. 9 I have smitten you with blasting and mildew: when your gardens and your vineyards and your fig trees and your olive trees increased, the palmerworm devoured them: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the LORD. 10 I have sent among you the pestilence after the manner of Egypt: your young men have I slain with the sword, and have taken away your horses; and I have made the stink of your camps to come up unto your nostrils: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the LORD. 11 I have overthrown some of you, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and ye were as a firebrand plucked out of the burning: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the LORD.

He enumerated for them the chastisements that He allowed them to fall under, and yet they did not benefit from them, for each time He punishes, saying: "Yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the LORD" [6, 8-11]. It is as though chastisement in the eyes of God is not vengeance for Himself but love... He desires man's return to Him.

If the previous chastisements, with all their multitude and variety, did not achieve their goal because of the hardness of man's heart, then He is bound to present a harsher chastisement, so that man may recover from his drunkenness, come to know God and prepare to meet Him: "And because I will do this unto thee, prepare to meet thy God, O Israel" [12]. Perhaps this phrase is the key to the whole book, indeed the key to the whole Holy Bible: all that God does with His people, whether kindness or firmness, leniency or severity, is so that it may prepare to meet its God, who comes down to it to dwell in it and to sanctify it as a people for Himself!
What are the chastisements that God allowed to His people?

"And I also have given you cleanness (idleness, or ceasing from work) of teeth in all your cities, and want of bread in all your places" [6]. Their teeth became clean because they were deprived of chewing and eating, so that nothing at all entered their mouths! In the Septuagint: "Their teeth became idle, without work..." as though likened to the idle man who is of no use to himself or to others.

His saying "I have given you" indicates that what happens of natural disasters, which cause famines until their teeth become clean through disuse, does not happen by mere chance, but by a precise divine plan and a surpassing heavenly providence. Moreover, what happens is the gift of God, "I have given you": He bestows good things as He grants distress, trials and famines. In His love He is gentle with us and satisfies us, and in His wisdom He deprives us and chastises us so that we return to Him.
The trials and chastisements that He allows reveal by them the work of sin in us and its hidden fruit within us, for it causes:

First: famines, "want of bread in all your places" [6]. Perhaps He meant by it the famine that occurred in the days of the prophet Elisha and lasted seven years (2 Kgs 8:1). Thus sin drives to a spiritual famine, so that man is in want of spiritual bread in all his inner life. He lives without satisfaction, in a great emptiness that no one can fill except the Lord Himself, the Bread that came down from heaven (Jn 6:51).

Second: spiritual dryness. "And also I have withholden the rain from you, when there were yet three months to the harvest: and I caused it to rain upon one city, and caused it not to rain upon another city... So two or three cities wandered unto one city, to drink water; but they were not satisfied" [7-8]. When the soul rejects the fountain of living waters (Jer 2:13), that is, Christ the Savior, it is deprived of the rain of the Holy Spirit and remains in a state of dryness! Two neighboring cities, one of which is watered by the rain of the Spirit and the other dries up; two villages or fields in one city, one field watered by the grace of the Spirit and the other remaining dry! Thus the world includes various hearts: some that open to the gift of the fiery Spirit to be set aflame by Him and to bear the heavenly nature, and others that close in upon themselves to live in their dryness, dead in spirit, enjoying nothing but barrenness and destruction! As the Lord says: "Behold, my servants shall eat, but ye shall be hungry: behold, my servants shall drink, but ye shall be thirsty: behold, my servants shall rejoice, but ye shall be ashamed: Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart, but ye shall cry for sorrow of heart, and shall howl for vexation of spirit" (Isa 65:13-14).

What are the two or three cities that wandered to one city to drink water and were not satisfied but the foolish virgins who ask the wise ones for oil lest their lamps go out, and the wise answer: "Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you" (Mt 25:9), so they go outside the wedding and the door is shut against them!

Third: the smiting with destructive insects such as blasting, mildew and locusts, which eat the fruits of the soul, corrupt its inner garden and rule over its vines and fig trees... We have already spoken at greater length about the campaigns of the locusts, the vines and the fig trees in our study of the book of Joel.

If the soul is the inner paradise, or the garden in whose spiritual vines and fig trees God delights, then sin, like an insect, turns paradise into a wilderness and the fruit trees into a rugged waste!

Fourth: the pestilence that afflicts soul and body together, which puts man in a state of sickness, lying on his bed without strength and unable to work! He needs the Savior, the true Physician of the soul!
Fifth: the slaying of their young men with the sword, that is, the shattering of man's gifts (his children) and energies.

Sixth: the taking away of their horses. If the horse signifies strength and might, then when man commits sin he loses his mastery over himself and becomes a captive without strength or freedom of action!

Seventh: the stink of their camps coming up into their nostrils... Instead of man bearing the sweet fragrance of Christ, which gladdens the Father's heart and delights the heavenly ones, the stench of the odor of his own inner self wafts from man, as though he were a dead man who has begun to stink! He needs to hear the voice of our Lord Jesus: "Lazarus, come forth," and the dead man who stinks comes out of his tomb bearing the fragrance of life instead of death!

Eighth: destruction by earthquakes and volcanoes: "I have overthrown some of you, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and ye were as a firebrand plucked out of the burning" [11]. He threatened all by casting some into the fires through thunderbolts and volcanoes, and plucked some out that they might repent, yet they did not return to Him... Instead of volcanoes and thunderbolts destroying us with their deadly fires, we have need that the Lord enter into us, as on a swift, light cloud, to shatter our inner idols, burn our evils and set up in the midst of our heart an altar for Himself, as the prophet Isaiah said in speaking of the Lord who rides swiftly on the cloud to the land of Egypt (Isa 19:1).
